title: Refinement of compactifications
statement:
Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] and let
$c=(X\xrightarrow{j}\overline X\xrightarrow{p}S)$ and
$c'=(X\xrightarrow{j'}\overline X'\xrightarrow{p'}S)$ be compactifications of
$f$ in the sense of [def-nagata-compactification], with $j,j'$ quasi-compact [def-weil-finite-type-morphism]
open immersions [def-weil-open-immersion]. A *refinement* $h:c'\to c$ is a morphism of schemes
$h:\overline X'\to\overline X$ such that

1. $p\circ h=p'$ ($h$ is an $S$-morphism [def-weil-scheme-over-base]);
1. $h\circ j'=j$ ($h$ is compatible with the identifications of $X$ with the
   opens $j'(X)\subseteq\overline X'$ and $j(X)\subseteq\overline X$);
1. $h^{-1}(j(X))=j'(X)$ as open subschemes of $\overline X'$.

Here $h^{-1}(j(X))$ denotes the open subscheme on the inverse image of the underlying open subset $j(X)$, with its restricted structure sheaf. Boundaries denote complements of the underlying open subsets, without a chosen closed subscheme structure.

By the second condition, $h$ restricts on $j'(X)$ to the isomorphism
$j\circ(j')^{-1}:j'(X)\xrightarrow{\sim}j(X)$, so the third condition says
that $h$ maps the boundary $\overline X'\setminus j'(X)$ into the boundary
$\overline X\setminus j(X)$. Refinements compose: if $h:c'\to c$ and
$h':c''\to c'$ are refinements, then $p\circ h\circ h'=p''$,
$h\circ h'\circ j''=h\circ j'=j$, and
$(h\circ h')^{-1}(j(X))=h'^{-1}(j'(X))=j''(X)$; the identity of
$\overline X$ is a refinement $c\to c$. Compactifications of $f$ whose open immersions are quasi-compact, with their
refinements, thus form a category [def-nagata-category], and the *dense* compactifications
([def-nagata-dense-compactification]) form a full subcategory: its objects are the dense compactifications and its morphisms between any two of these objects are all the refinements in the ambient category.

proof.text: Write $U=j(X)$ and $U'=j'(X)$. By [def-weil-open-immersion], the maps $j:X\to U$ and $j':X\to U'$ are isomorphisms. The equation $h\circ j'=j$ therefore identifies the restriction of $h$ to $U'$ with $j\circ(j')^{-1}$. In particular $U'\subseteq h^{-1}(U)$. The equality $h^{-1}(U)=U'$ is consequently equivalent to saying that every point outside $U'$ maps outside $U$. Equality here is also equality of open subschemes, since both carry the restricted structure sheaf on the same open subset. This proves the stated boundary interpretation without assigning scheme structures to the complements.

source.place: paragraph beginning By the second condition

proof.text: For any object $c$, the identity on $\overline X$ satisfies $p\circ\mathrm{id}=p$, $\mathrm{id}\circ j=j$, and $\mathrm{id}^{-1}(j(X))=j(X)$. Thus it satisfies all three defining conditions for a refinement $c\to c$.

For refinements $h:c'\to c$ and $h':c''\to c'$, associativity gives $p\circ(h\circ h')=(p\circ h)\circ h'=p'\circ h'=p''$ and $(h\circ h')\circ j''=h\circ(h'\circ j'')=h\circ j'=j$. On underlying open subsets, $(h\circ h')^{-1}(j(X))=(h')^{-1}(h^{-1}(j(X)))=(h')^{-1}(j'(X))=j''(X)$. All these opens have the restricted structure sheaf, so the last equality is an equality of open subschemes. The composite therefore satisfies all three defining conditions.

source.place: last paragraph, Refinements compose and its three displayed identities

proof.text: Use compactifications with quasi-compact open immersion as objects, the prescribed scheme morphisms satisfying the three conditions as morphisms, and the identity and composition of Steps 2 and 3. The category of schemes in [def-pc-scheme] supplies the identity and associativity equalities for these underlying morphisms. Since a refinement contains just an underlying morphism with properties, these equalities are equalities of refinements, giving exactly the category axioms [def-nagata-category]. Restrict the objects to compactifications satisfying [def-nagata-dense-compactification] and leave each morphism set unchanged. Identities and composites remain those already constructed, and the inclusion is the identity on each morphism set; this is the full subcategory asserted in the statement. No density preservation theorem is required.

source.place: last sentence, category and full subcategory clauses
